community: Remote & backcountry, Regional District of Kitimat-Stikine

description.value: Kinaskan Lake Provincial Park offers lakeshore camping on a remote northern lake along the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37), with potable water and washrooms on-site; the site is popular with anglers and operates on a short summer season in a genuinely wild Stikine setting.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content returned only BC Parks navigation menus with no park-specific amenity text, so OSM tags are the primary evidence source. OSM tags are detailed and explicit: drinking_water=yes, shower=no, toilets=yes, laundry=no, power_supply=no, tents=yes, picnic_table=yes, openfire=yes, and internet_access=no. The operator field names a private individual (Margaret Klocker) with an xplornet email while the linked website is the official BC Parks page, suggesting a concession-operated arrangement within Kinaskan Lake Provincial Park.
concerns: OSM operator is a private individual (Margaret Klocker, rnmklocker@xplornet.com) but the linked website is the official BC Parks page — the phone number may reach the concessionaire rather than BC Parks central reservations; worth clarifying.
Website content fetched was entirely navigation menus with no park-specific text; no amenity details could be confirmed from the website itself.
OSM lists mobile_reception=no and internet_access=no, which is notable context for cyclists but could not be verified via website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, operational provincial park campground on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway with 50 sites; directly relevant to touring cyclists on this remote corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: Campground is located on Highway 37 (Stewart-Cassiar Highway) in a very remote area; nearest resupply may be Dease Lake (~90 km north) or Iskut. Campfires permitted per OSM openfire=yes.

wow_evidence: lakeshore camping along the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37), with potable water and washrooms on-site; genuinely wild Stikine setting
